section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Harmonic Series and Convergence
section_1.content: Establish the foundation by looking at the p-series. Explain how the series 1/n^s converges only when s > 1, setting the stage for the definition of the Zeta function.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'Zeno's Paradox' scenario: An ant traveling halfway to a cookie, then a quarter, then an eighth. Summing these distances converges to 1 (the cookie).

section_2.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
section_2.content: Formally introduce ζ(s) = Σ 1/n^s. Explain that for s > 1, this is a standard sum, but for other complex values, we must use 'Analytic Continuation' to extend its domain.
section_2.example: An animation showing a map expanding: starting with a small 'real' island, then drawing lines into the 'complex' ocean (the complex plane) to reveal the full landmass.

section_3.title: The Magic Connection: Euler Product Formula
section_3.content: Demonstrate the bridge between the Zeta function and Prime Numbers. Show the equivalence between the summation of integers and the infinite product of primes.
section_3.example: A sieve visual: A machine that sorts integers into their prime 'DNA' components, demonstrating how the Zeta function acts as a filter for prime numbers.

section_4.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Strip
section_4.content: Discuss the 'Critical Strip' (0 < Re(s) < 1). Introduce the Riemann Hypothesis: all non-trivial zeros lie on the line Re(s) = 1/2. Explain its significance to prime number distribution.
section_4.example: A radar display: The Zeta function is represented as a wave. The zeros are 'pings' on the radar. The Hypothesis predicts they all align perfectly on a single vertical laser beam.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Impact
section_5.content: Summarize why this is the 'Holy Grail' of mathematics: understanding the 'music' of prime numbers. Acknowledge that a proof remains the most elusive prize in math.
section_5.example: A closing shot of a giant library where the bookshelf containing the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is the only one locked, waiting for the next generation to find the key.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right
